meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.title: A sensor/autophagy biomarker panel as a surrogate endpoint for human trials
data.gap: QUANTIFIED human-endpoint desert: every completed human trial in this corpus with a clinical or functional aging/healthspan PRIMARY endpoint missed it or was safety-only. The exception is immune-response surrogates, which were met: MAN2014 (influenza-vaccine response, about 20%) and the MAN2018 phase 2a (self-reported infections) - which is why H7 reports positive human data while this card reports none on hard outcomes. PEARL (MOE2025): visceral fat NOT met (secondary bone density OR 0.24, 95% CI 0.06-0.93, p=0.04). RTB101 phase 3 (MAN2021): symptomatic-RTI primary NOT met. Resveratrol (POU2013): fully negative. CALERIE (ROM2016): the paper held here is the SAFETY analysis of the two-year randomised caloric-restriction trial in 218 non-obese adults - CR was safe and well tolerated overall, but bone density fell significantly more than in controls, so 'no significant differences' would be wrong. Scope note: CALERIE is a caloric-restriction trial, not an mTOR-inhibitor trial; it belongs here as a geroscience comparator, not as direct evidence on an mTOR intervention. The human 'wins' are disease indications (BOLERO-2 / BAS2012: PFS roughly doubled with exemestane, overall survival not significantly improved; RADIANT-3 / YAO2011: median PFS 11.0 vs 4.6 months, HR 0.35, p<0.001) or surrogate biomarkers (CHU2019: topical rapamycin epidermal p16 reduced, p=0.008). Not 'few trials' but none with a hard aging endpoint. On the assay side, a live-cell readout exists for mTORC1-associated signalling -- AIMTOR (BOU2020), a genetically encoded BRET biosensor characterised in cell lines and in primary myoblasts from a single human muscle biopsy, which reads mTOR activity live with subcellular resolution (lysosome/cytosol/nucleus/mitochondria). Its scope is narrower than this panel needs. The authors report that it responds mainly to mTORC1, that rapamycin and the pan-mTOR inhibitor Torin1 lowered the signal to a similar degree, and that contributions from mTORC2 or other PIKK-family kinases cannot be ruled out; the signal also integrates endogenous phosphatase activity alongside mTOR kinase activity. So it is a working assay for mTORC1-associated signalling in cells engineered to carry it, not a validated blood panel that distinguishes mTORC1 from mTORC2, and it does not remove the assay-development step from this question.
data.gap_beginner: Among the human trials collected in this Atlas, none has shown a clinical or functional healthspan benefit: trials aimed at such outcomes either missed their main goal or only checked safety. The goals that were met are immune-response measures, such as a better flu-vaccine response in older adults, not proof of healthier or longer lives. The wins that do exist are for specific diseases (like certain cancers), not for ageing itself. Testing ageing directly takes decades, so researchers want a faster stand-in measurement. A tool that tracks mTOR activity live inside cells does exist, but it has to be built into the cells first, and it cannot tell the two mTOR complexes apart – so the blood test this question asks for still has to be developed and validated.
data.changed_since_written: The field has explicitly separated three things this question merges: a target-engagement marker, a biomarker of ageing, and a validated surrogate endpoint (Moqri, Cell 2023, PMID 37657418). The 2025 Longevity Biotechnology Association recommendations for trial biomarkers list clocks, omics and functional measures, and do not include a pathway-activity panel (Herzog, npj Aging 2025, PMID 41436473). The current answer to shortening geroscience trials is hierarchical clinical composites with biomarkers placed at the lowest tier (Abdellatif, Nature Aging 2026, PMID 42342910), alongside organ-specific proteomic clocks (Goeminne, Cell Metab 2024, PMID 39488213). On this panel's own components: there is no human blood assay for SAMTOR or GATOR state in this corpus, and the earliest measurement of physiological autophagic flux in a large human trial that this Atlas holds reached significance only post hoc (Bensalem, J Physiol 2025, PMID 40345145, n=121, six months). A second intervention-responsive human readout has since reported: in a placebo-controlled experimental-medicine study in older adults, low-dose rapamycin significantly reduced p21, a marker of DNA-damage-induced senescence, in immune cells (Kell, Aging Cell 2026, PMID 41524558). That is a pharmacodynamic marker moving under controlled conditions, and nothing links it to clinical benefit.
data.still_open: Split in two, because the halves have different answers. As a pharmacodynamic readout for choosing dose and schedule, an mTORC1 against mTORC2 substrate panel is tractable and trials are running. As a surrogate endpoint it is not: surrogacy requires showing the marker mediates clinical benefit across intervention classes, and no ageing biomarker of any kind — pathway panel, epigenetic clock or organ clock — has met that bar. The consensus papers say so themselves.
data.hypothesis: Two hypotheses. Tractable: a blood mTORC1/mTORC2 substrate-phosphorylation panel plus an autophagic-flux assay can select dose and schedule for mTOR-directed geroprotectors in humans. Still negative: that any ageing biomarker satisfies formal surrogate-endpoint criteria sufficient for regulatory acceptance.
data.hypothesis_beginner: Two different claims that were being treated as one. The easier one: blood tests can show the drug is hitting the pathway, which helps pick a dose. The hard one, still unmet: a blood test that stands in for living longer or healthier, well enough that a regulator would accept it instead of waiting.
data.how_to_test: Back-test the panel across the animal longevity studies in the corpus (does it separate lifespan-extending from null interventions?), then validate prospectively against EVERLAST's daily-vs-weekly arms. The mTORC1-vs-mTORC2 substrate-phosphorylation arm still requires assay development, and the experiment has to name it: state the biological variable each readout measures, validate complex specificity independently rather than assuming it, and fix sample processing, dynamic-range calibration and prospective clinical validation before any panel is read as a pharmacodynamic marker. AIMTOR (BOU2020) can inform that development but does not supply it. It is a genetically encoded reporter that must be expressed in cells rather than applied to an unmodified blood sample; in the primary paper rapamycin and the pan-mTOR inhibitor Torin1 lowered its signal to a similar degree, so it does not resolve mTORC1 from mTORC2; and the authors state they cannot rule out contributions from mTORC2 or other PIKK-family kinases. Because the reporter also integrates endogenous phosphatase activity alongside kinase activity, no equal-AIMTOR-average result may be described as proof of equal integrated kinase catalysis - a constraint that applies to the matched-average proposals in F1-F3 as well.
revision_log: 2026-07-09: AIMTOR (BOU2020) biosensor added as a candidate readout.
2026-08-30: The basis previously cited RADIANT-3 (YAO2011) as 'PFS 5% vs 2%'. Those were the grade 3/4 hyperglycaemia rates from the adverse-event table, not a progression-free-survival result.
2026-09-04: Trial acronyms paired with Atlas study codes inline.
2026-09-23: The hypothesis was split in two (it was previously one).
2026-09-29: 'Every trial missed' limited to clinical and functional healthspan endpoints; the immune-response surrogates that were met (MAN2014, MAN2018) are now named.

2026-10-03: KAN2013 added - shows in human and mouse cell lines that individual mTORC1 phosphorylation sites differ in intrinsic substrate quality and therefore in their sensitivity to rapamycin and starvation, which constrains how a substrate-phosphorylation panel can be read as a pharmacodynamic marker (cell lines, not human blood).

2026-10-03: SIN2026 added - a randomised crossover trial in 63 healthy young adults found no change in whole-blood LC3B-II autophagic flux after 4 weeks of reduced (10%) vs average (20%) protein intake, showing a human flux assay is feasible but did not respond to moderate protein restriction (human, PBMCs only; mTORC1 not measured).

2026-10-03: MAN2014 and MAN2018 added to Supporting_Studies. They were named in the basis on 2026-09-29 as the two met endpoints but never linked, so the card cited evidence the reader could not open (validate_claims.py R10).

2026-10-05: MOR2026 added (daily check, unreviewed) - a healthy-aging human cohort study found PBMC autophagic flux is measurable, cell type- and sex-specific, associates with reduced physical function after age 70, and decreases over 12 weeks of mild exercise in parallel with improved function, further strengthening the case that an autophagic-flux readout is a feasible, intervention-responsive human assay (human, observational + pilot intervention, not a validated surrogate endpoint).

2026-10-07: KEL2026 (PMID 41524558) added - p21 in immune cells as a human PD readout that responded to low-dose rapamycin under placebo control. Strengthens the pharmacodynamic half of the split; the surrogate half is unchanged (revision of all 17 cards against the literature).

2026-10-10: Audit N04. The card treated AIMTOR (BOU2020) as a ready-made readout for the mTORC1-versus-mTORC2 arm of the panel, so that arm 'can now build directly on AIMTOR rather than needing de novo assay development'. Checked against the primary full text: AIMTOR is a genetically encoded reporter requiring expression in the cell, it responds mainly to mTORC1, rapamycin and Torin1 lower its signal to a similar degree so it does not resolve the two complexes, the authors cannot exclude mTORC2 or other PIKK kinases, and the signal integrates phosphatase as well as kinase activity. The human material was primary myoblasts from one muscle biopsy, not blood. The assay-development step is back in the proposed experiment, with specificity, sample processing, dynamic range and prospective validation named, and the phosphatase constraint on matched-average readings is now stated.
